verdictBasis: The response materially improves DELIVERY: protocol-major 1 now has sixteen closed outer payload schemas, one typed multi-stage Analyze transaction, exact process ownership and atomicity, and the scanner rejection now agrees with REQUEST-ID-V1 and D9. IP-R4-05 therefore PASSes, and independent enumeration of live C-2 proves the fourteen-axis v1 overlay plus all twenty-one fixtures are total, so R7-C2-03 PASSes. IP-R4-03 still FAILs. DELIVERY's own C-2-valid, overlay-allowed TypeScript fixture cannot be projected into StageRequestV1 without inventing mandatory dependsOn and budget values; the legal C-2 StageBudgetV1 is not the six-dimensional ProviderWorkBudgetV1 and even permits semantic milliseconds that DELIVERY forbids. Clean Unavailable/BudgetExhausted cannot construct their promised exhaustive per-stage/relation Coverage from the request for cross-universe relations, and the claimed FACT-IDENTITY join has neither a generic FactEnvelope.factId recipe nor bound relation payload schemas. The retained checker also raises AttributeError for the exact former ordering mutation and every tested scalar substitution at the wire-schema nodes instead of returning deterministic findings. These are design-integrity and implementability findings; no product behavior was evaluated or demonstrated.

IP-R4-05.why: An external-scanner selector on either C-2 surface deterministically rejects during request-validation. REQUEST-ID-V1 is allocated and reserved before parsing, RequestId is present and semantically inert, every attempt/Snapshot/Plan/Run identity is absent, and the typed product reason projects through D9 extension-admission-rejected / EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED without extending D9. Exact former probes 09 and 10 now reject.

R7-C2-03.why: Independent source-enum derivation found exact key equality for all fourteen live C-2 axes. A separately written overlay evaluator reproduced all nineteen denials and both positive controls after every mutated intent validated under live C-2. The future-enum guard, common zero-attempt fate, RequestId fate and D9 projection are exact.
R7-C2-03.qualification: R5R-DLTS-05 is a separate cross-contract provider-identifier contradiction. It does not make the overlay partial—the overlay deterministically denies the provider.* values—but it does invalidate the current C-2/RI artifact's label that its prefixed-provider fixture is the v1 full-profile oracle.

independentProbes.axis: protocol payload and multi-stage outer shape
independentProbes.detail: Sixteen frame schemas form a bijection with sixteen closed payload schemas: seven host-to-worker and nine worker-to-host. Required/optional fields partition every payload field exactly; the eight closed nested record definitions have unique required fields. All thirteen typed multiStageAnalyze constants match the declared one-worker/one-Analyze/logical-order/non-interleaved/bijection/atomic model.
independentProbes.qualification: Closed outer shape does not establish that every field is constructible from the live inputs; probes 03 through 05 falsify that stronger response claim.

independentProbes.counterexample: Apply DELIVERY fixture allow-bundled-typescript-provider. Live C-2 returns zero validation errors and the overlay expects ALLOW. Its exact stage is {kind:fact-derivation, stageId:s1, relations:[declares], operator:semantic-provider, providerId:typescript-semantic}; it has neither dependsOn nor budget. StageRequestV1 nevertheless requires both. C-2 also accepts budget={unit:milliseconds,limit:1}; ProviderWorkBudgetV1 instead requires six unrelated maxima and DELIVERY says provider wall clock is never a semantic budget.
independentProbes.contradiction: multiStageAnalyze.ordering says dependsOn and budget are copied exactly, while the wire requires an absent-to-array normalization and a different budget type.

independentProbes.counterexample: Unavailable is legal only immediately after Analyze and promises exactly one unknown CoverageResultV1 per requested stage/relation. CoverageKeyV1 simultaneously requires resolution, exact targetUniverseId and exact subjectScopeCommitment. StageRequestV1 carries relations but no requested Coverage-key domain, subject set or target-universe partition. C-2 explicitly marks imports, calls and references cross-universe. A provider unavailable because resolution inputs are missing cannot enumerate the exact target partitions whose absence caused the terminal, and one entry per relation cannot represent multiple target universes.
independentProbes.additionalLimit: Normal success permits exactly one Coverage frame per stage with at most 4096 entries but defines no semantic fate if the exhaustive target/subject partition needs more entries.

independentProbes.counterexample: FACT-PLANE declares factId only as ContentDigest and closes FactEnvelope to its nine required plus two optional fields. It does not define a FactId preimage. FACT-IDENTITY's opensip.fact-identity.v1 byte grammar hashes a normalized body span beginning at L0 boundaries; it is not a generic full-FactEnvelope recipe. FactCandidateV1 adds source/target universes, relationSchemaId, opaque canonicalRelationPayload and multiple anchors, but no binding artifact defines the referenced relation schemas or how those fields map into the closed FactEnvelope and its identity.

newFindings.title: StageRequestV1 is not a total projection of a DELIVERY-allowed C-2 TypeScript stage
newFindings.evidence: C-2 makes dependsOn and StageBudgetV1 optional. DELIVERY's own allow-bundled-typescript-provider fixture is C-2-valid without either, while StageRequestV1 requires both. Where a stage budget exists it is closed {unit,limit}, with unit work-units|milliseconds|bytes|items. ProviderWorkBudgetV1 is six mandatory maxima. No default, allocation, conversion, rejection or per-unit mapping exists, and multiStageAnalyze says the incompatible budget is copied exactly.
newFindings.impact: The host must invent empty dependency normalization, budget defaults and a one-to-six budget translation. Different choices change whether/when BudgetExhausted occurs and therefore change Coverage and the Run verdict. A legal milliseconds budget directly conflicts with DELIVERY's rule that wall clock cannot define semantic provider exhaustion.
newFindings.requiredChange: Bind one total Plan/PlanIntent-to-StageRequest projection. Specify absent dependsOn normalization; select the authoritative source for every provider budget dimension; define defaults and exact unit conversions or reject unsupported C-2 budget units in the v1 overlay; add positive vectors for absent and present budgets and negative vectors for every unmappable value.

newFindings.category: fact admission identity and body schema
newFindings.title: The FactCandidate host join cites a generic FACT-IDENTITY recipe and relation schemas that do not exist
newFindings.evidence: FactCandidateV1 says the host canonicalises the full fact envelope and mints/verifies factId under FACT-IDENTITY. FACT-PLANE only says factId is a ContentDigest; it publishes no preimage/framing/algorithm recipe and its closed envelope has no relation payload, source/target universe or anchor fields. FACT-IDENTITY's published recipe is specifically the normalized body-span ladder. relationSchemaId is arbitrary non-empty text resolving inside a future provider artifact; no binding registry or schemas are present.
newFindings.impact: The JavaScript producer, Rust host, store and pure evaluation core must invent the semantic fact body, host validation API and FactId preimage. Two conforming implementations can produce different facts and identifiers from identical source and PlanId, defeating deterministic admission, cache identity and evidence references.
newFindings.requiredChange: Assign ownership and bind a versioned registry of v1 relation payload schemas, the exact candidate-to-admitted-fact mapping, and a domain-separated generic FactId preimage with independent vectors. If the generic recipe belongs in FACT-PLANE rather than FACT-IDENTITY, change DELIVERY's join to that exact contract and keep body-normalization identity separate.

newFindings.title: Unavailable and BudgetExhausted cannot construct their promised exact C-2 Coverage domain
newFindings.evidence: Each failure terminal promises exactly one CoverageResultV1 per stage/relation. Each key requires a resolution, exact source and target universe, and an exact subjectScopeCommitment, while completeness promises an exhaustive subject/target partition. Analyze carries no requested key/partition set. For C-2's cross-universe imports/calls/references, one relation can require distinct targets, and immediate Unavailable may be caused by the missing resolution data needed to identify them.
newFindings.impact: A worker can fabricate a target, omit partitions, emit more than one entry despite the one-per-pair rule, or fail the protocol. Each choice changes whether downstream predicates see honest unknown Coverage. The 4096-entry single-Coverage-frame limit also has no semantic overflow fate.
newFindings.requiredChange: Have the host derive and send the exact requested Coverage domain/subject-scope commitment and define cardinality per full CoverageKey or partition, not merely per relation; alternatively revise the C-2 failure key so typed unknown targets are representable. Specify deterministic overflow behavior and add cross-universe Unavailable/BudgetExhausted vectors with multiple target partitions.

newFindings.title: check-delivery.py is not total over legal JSON with wrong protocol-schema types
newFindings.evidence: The exact former R5-PROBE-08 ordering string raises AttributeError. All sixteen scalar payload-schema substitutions, all eight scalar nested-definition substitutions and five scalar wire-container substitutions also raise AttributeError. The retained selftest uses a different nested stageOrder mutation, so 62/62 remains green.
newFindings.impact: The checker has no deterministic finding for a broad hostile/wrong-schema input class. Automation sees an uncategorized exception and the mutation suite overstates closure of R5-DLTS-03.
newFindings.requiredChange: Type-guard every container before .get, set, iteration or equality logic; make check() a total function over parsed JSON; retain the exact permissive-ordering string and representative scalar/null/array/object substitutions at each schema layer.

newFindings.title: The live C-2/RI v1 full-profile oracle uses provider IDs that DELIVERY necessarily denies
newFindings.evidence: C-2's valid-full-profile-semantic-providers fixture is valid, committed and labelled V1 FULL PROFILE; RI's full-provider PlanId vector consumes it. Its provider IDs are provider.rust-semantic and provider.typescript-semantic. DELIVERY allows/selects only rust-semantic and typescript-semantic, so the overlay deterministically denies the fixture and the TypeScript stage selector cannot select it.
newFindings.impact: The binding v1 full-profile PlanIntent/PlanId oracle cannot reach either bundled semantic provider. An implementer must choose whether to rename C-2/RI records or broaden DELIVERY, changing committed identities and admission behavior.
newFindings.requiredChange: Choose one canonical provider-id namespace across C-2 PlanIntent contributions/stages, RI semanticUniverses, DELIVERY profile manifests/overlay/protocol and all commitment vectors; regenerate affected commitments and add one joined v1 full-profile admission-to-provider-selection vector.
newFindings.r7Qualification: This is not an unclassified overlay value and therefore does not reverse the narrow R7-C2-03 totality PASS. It is a separate contradiction in which artifact is the canonical allowed v1 full-profile input.

Protocol-major 1 has a closed deterministic-CBOR frame vocabulary, closed outer payload field sets, exact byte/count limits, stream commitments and a coherent one-Analyze atomic state machine.

The wire-schema and overlay commitments independently reproduce byte-for-byte.
